body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/37379
Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/3488

## What changed

- Added external FP8 KV-scale loading to the actual Qwen3.5 dense and MoE causal classes and delegated it through both conditional-generation wrappers.
- Preserved validation by mapping the nested `*_text` config type to the public calibration model type instead of disabling the model-type check.
- Extended the shared schema loader to validate the exact set of KV-bearing attention layers, allowing hybrid Qwen3.5 calibration files to omit GatedDeltaNet SSM layers without accepting missing or extra attention scales.
- Loaded rank-specific values into `k_scale`, `v_scale`, `k_scale_float`, and `v_scale_float` and covered the real Triton descale consumer.
- Added retained failing-before, unit-test, and AMD FP8 numerical evidence under `reports/j-25a3b89d4e8d/`.

## Reproduction and validation

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-25a3b89d4e8d/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_kv_cache_scales.py \
  test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_pipeline_parallel.py
```

Result: 10 passed and 6 subtests passed.

Repository pre-commit checks passed for every changed source/test/report file. On one AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015, FP8 E4M3 quantize/dequantize output using scale 0.5 exactly matched an independent CPU reference.

## Limitations

The exact reported Qwen3.5-122B-A10B deployment on eight NVIDIA L20 GPUs with TP=8 was unavailable and remains unverified. Model weights were also unavailable, so this does not claim full server startup, distributed execution, or semantic output validation. The AMD check qualifies supported gfx950 FP8 execution plus the model-loading/downstream-consumer unit path only. No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
